contributions.statement: If a code model is ever fine-tuned on a few hundred examples, compare a sparse layer-selected LoRA against all-layer LoRA and the untuned model before trusting the all-layer result, because restricting updates to about 6 of 48 blocks scored 22.9-29.7% vs 18.9% pass@1 for all-block LoRA on 175 LiveCodeBench tasks.
contributions.evidence: Table 1: Qwen-LCB Rand-K6 22.86, Model-Only 24.00, CKA-K6 24.57, CogAdapt 29.71 vs Regular FT 18.86; smaller and mixed on BigCodeBench (CKA-K6 32.73 below Regular FT 36.36). Caveats: single pass per condition, no untuned base reported, two MoE models, Python only; the team does not train models.
relative_to: LISA and CKA-based layer-wise LoRA selection (Pan et al. 2024; Ogawa et al. 2026)

reason: A weight fine-tuning method for MoE code models has no use for a team that drives hosted models through agent hosts. The 'EEG prior' reduces to a ridge regression over static code-size metrics, sparsity alone explains about half of the headline gain, and every number is one pass without an untuned base. Nothing here informs a harness, spec or onboarding decision.
